newsitem.title: DENMARK: Kleinwort Benson says sell Tele Danmark.
newsitem.headline: Kleinwort Benson says sell Tele Danmark.

text.p: Investment bank Kleinwort Benson is advising clients to sell stock in telecoms group Tele Danmark, saying rumours that BT (British Telecom) seeks a stake in the Danish firm are unfounded.

In an analysis received by Reuters on Friday Kleinwort added that new Danish regulations on mobile phone traffic and forthcoming deregulation in Belgium, where Tele Danmark owns 16.5 percent of Belgacom, could also hurt the share.

"We believe rumours that BT may buy a stake in Tele Danmark are without ground. Instead we feel market sentiment remains vulnerable to the impact of growing fixed/mobile competition, fresh question marks over cellular interconnection rates and growing uncertainty over Belgacom's future growth," it said.

Market talk that BT might bid for some of the Danish state's 51 percent stake in Tele Danmark if, as expected, the government reduces its holding, sent the Danish group's share up to its current 356 crowns from 321 on June 3, before the rumours began.
Tele Danmark said on June 6 that it had had no contact with BT and knew nothing of any plans to buy a stake.
The Kleinwort study said that Tele Danmark's price to cashflow ratio of 6.4x was the second highest in the sector after Portugal Telecom's 6.7x and well above the sector average of 5.3x.

It added that partially state-owned Belgacom was likely to be hard-pressed by the introduction next year of competition as its tariffs were high, it had no major allies to help fight bigger rivals and it was encumbered by a 120 billion Belgian franc unfunded pension liability. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33 969650
